edges.description: Coagulation factors and their inhibitors are N-glycoproteins, so reduced glycosylation-site occupancy disturbs haemostasis directly. This is the standard route by which type I CDG produce coagulopathy, and in the index patient the disturbance was prothrombotic and ultimately fatal.
intermediate_mechanisms: Hypoglycosylation of hepatically synthesized coagulation factors and their regulators, which are N-glycoproteins

edges.description: The thrombotic events are the clinical consequence of the coagulopathy: the index patient's abnormal coagulation caused thrombosis and death from pulmonary embolism.
intermediate_mechanisms: Prothrombotic coagulopathy from hypoglycosylated coagulation factors and inhibitors (curated as the Coagulopathy phenotype)

edges.description: The glycosylation disorder acts prenatally: the index report describes a severe disorder affecting intrauterine development and leading to growth restriction. Which hypoglycosylated proteins mediate the prenatal growth failure is not known.
The index report describes the disorder as affecting intrauterine movement, and the child was born with arthrogryposis — the classical consequence of reduced fetal movement.
intermediate_mechanisms: Impaired fetal movement in utero (fetal akinesia), which produces congenital joint contractures

edges.description: Drug-resistant early-onset epilepsy is a core manifestation of the severe neurological syndrome. No seizure-specific molecular mechanism has been described in RFT1-CDG.
Deafness occurs as part of the severe neurological syndrome in almost all patients; which cochlear glycoproteins are affected is unknown.
Severely limited psychomotor development is central to the neurological disease across the reported cohort.
Decreased visual acuity to absent vision accompanies the neurological syndrome in most reported patients.
Hypotonia is present in every reported patient and is typically the presenting neurological sign.
Cerebellar dysfunction at the milder end of the neurological spectrum, in patients without epilepsy or deafness.
Reduced head growth in a subset of patients, reflecting the impact of the disease on brain growth.
Progressive supratentorial volume loss on serial imaging is the structural correlate of the neurological disease in one well-documented patient.
Posterior fossa hypoplasia in the lethal neonatal presentation, reflecting a prenatal effect of the disease on brain development.

Ventilatory failure at the lethal end of the spectrum, presenting in floppy neonates and consistent with neuromuscular weakness, though the precise mechanism of respiratory failure is not established.
Feeding problems severe enough to require gastrostomy are listed among the core neurological characteristics of the reported patients.
Postnatal growth failure driven by the gastrointestinal manifestations of the multisystem disease.
intermediate_mechanisms: Severe gastro-oesophageal reflux and disordered bowel motility
Feeding difficulties (curated as their own phenotype)

nodes.description: Because the pathway stalls, the truncated species Dol-PP-GlcNAc2Man5 accumulates intracellularly while the cytosolic free oligosaccharide GlcNAc2Man5 is absent. This paired pattern is the biochemical signature that first identified the defect and mirrors the profile of RFT1-null yeast.

nodes.description: Assembly of the N-glycosylation donor is a two-compartment process: the Man5GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol intermediate is built on the cytosolic face of the ER and must reach the lumen for the remaining mannose and glucose residues to be added. In RFT1 deficiency this transition fails, and the pathway stalls at the Man5 intermediate. The step itself is not in doubt; what RFT1 actually does at this step is, and the two readings are curated as competing hypotheses below.

nodes.description: Because N-glycosylation is required by a very large and functionally diverse set of secreted and membrane proteins, hypoglycosylation produces disease in many organs at once. In RFT1-CDG the burden falls most heavily on the nervous system and the ear: drug-resistant early-onset epilepsy, profound developmental impairment and visual failure, together with the sensorineural deafness that distinguishes this CDG from the others. Coagulation-factor hypoglycosylation adds a bleeding-and-thrombosis diathesis that proved fatal in the index case.

nodes.description: Serial imaging shows progressive loss of cortical and subcortical volume. Note the contrast with the pontocerebellar hypoplasia curated separately: the supratentorial change is progressive and acquired on serial MRI, whereas the infratentorial finding is a hypoplasia, and in the patient followed with serial scans the cerebellum was explicitly spared.

nodes.description: With the mature donor unavailable, the oligosaccharyltransferase reaction proceeds at reduced efficiency and sequons on nascent glycoproteins are left unoccupied. Site occupancy, rather than glycan structure, is what falls — which is why the defect presents biochemically as a CDG type I pattern on serum transferrin isoelectric focusing.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic RFT1 variants reduce or abolish the function of RFT1, a multispanning ER membrane protein whose N and C termini both face the cytoplasm. The index allele, c.199C>T (p.Arg67Cys), was shown to be functionally deleterious by complementation assay in RFT1-null yeast, and most RFT1-CDG alleles reported since fall in regions of the protein that are highly conserved across eukaryotes.

genetic_context.description: Reported genotypes are biallelic germline RFT1 variants, homozygous in the index case. Loss of function is established functionally: the index allele failed to complement RFT1-null yeast, and wild-type RFT1 cDNA restored normal glycosylation in patient fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Sensorineural hearing loss is the most discriminating feature of RFT1-CDG and is rarely reported across the CDG generally, which is why RFT1-CDG was designated the first "deafness-CDG" and why CDG entered the differential for syndromic congenital hearing loss. It is not, however, universal. It was present in all six patients in the report that established it, but later cases include two patients in whom deafness was absent, and adult siblings in whom hearing impairment affected only one of the pair. Treat it as the strongest single pointer to this diagnosis, not as a required feature.
